title: Harness Arena
moment: Saturday, 6:40am, a high-school track in October. Fog sits on the infield and lane one is still wet from the sprinklers. I am at the finish with a clipboard, a steel timer clipped to it, thumb resting on the button. Two runners are on the line, same distance, same heat, and nobody speaks. The scoreboard behind the stands is dark except one row. The number that counts is the one the watch prints, not what either of them says after.

light.source: low October sun behind fog, from the far end of the straight, left of camera
light.fill: one row of amber seven-segment digits glowing on a dark panel far behind the stands, 2000K, faint; a grey overcast skylight from above, 6500K, even

objects: steel timer, brushed steel and black rubber
two pairs of spikes, one orange one black
a timing sheet, cream paper, blue pen
inventory.sound: a radio hiss on the official's belt, then the click of the button
inventory.text: lane numbers stencilled on the track in white paint; split times written in blue ballpoint on a ruled sheet
inventory.gesture: thumb pressing the timer button at the mark
inventory.keepsake: the sheet with both times written in the same hand
inventory.utterance: Same line, same distance. The watch decides.
